## Observed Facts
Data Scope: BGL, whole period (2005-06-03 15:42:50 to 2006-01-04 08:00:05 [E1]), filter level = FATAL, grouped by component. There are 855,195 FATAL Log Entries in total [E2], spread across 4 Components:

| Component | FATAL Log Entries | Share of FATAL |
|---|---|---|
| KERNEL | 626,450 [E2] | about 73% |
| APP | 228,536 [E2] | about 27% |
| LINKCARD | 206 [E2] | under 0.1% |
| MMCS | 3 [E2] | negligible |

KERNEL and APP together account for nearly all FATAL Log Entries. These are counts of Log Entries, not incidents.

## Hypotheses
- A few repeating messages may make up most of the KERNEL and APP volume. That would make the counts reflect repetition more than many distinct problems. I haven't tested this.
- LINKCARD has few entries, but hardware-related FATAL entries can matter more than their count suggests.

## Unknowns
- I haven't checked whether the FATAL volume is steady or concentrated in bursts, because I haven't run a trend yet.
- I don't know which messages or nodes drive the KERNEL and APP counts.
- The logs can't tell me how many distinct incidents these entries represent.

## Next Step
Run a trend by day for FATAL KERNEL entries and for FATAL APP entries. Then group each by `node` and by message substring to see whether a few nodes or messages dominate. Investigate KERNEL first.
